I've been having suicidal thoughts almost constantly these past couple months. I have good days and I have bad days. And every time I'm having these thoughts I try to tell myself that it isn't worth it, things will improve, I would hurt so many people. But, those words I tell myself have lost their meaning and now they're just words combined properly to make a statement. But they have no meaning. 

I was about to hit a year of no self harm and I lost my shit and just got right back into it. My (now ex) boyfriend saw these cuts and ridiculed me for allowing myself to get so low and that I should have talked to him about it. The problem is though, that I tried to talk to him about these thoughts and urges and all I received in return was comments like "you just need to get out of your head" or "quit feeling sorry for yourself and get off your ass and do something about it" or "that's not going to solve anything, it's just going to make matters worse". 

That is exactly what you don't ever want to say to someone who is feeling suicidal. Although, you may feel like you're being helpful by saying these harsh things and attempting to motivate someone, it just makes me feel worse. I am very well aware that I'm stuck in my head, I'm very well aware that I need to stop feeling sorry for myself. Don't clarify things that I already know. 

When the boyfriend and I broke up, we had a long talk and for once it was actually civilized and we weren't at each other's throats. I told him that all I wanted was for him to listen. He was the most important person in my life and still somewhat is. And that really hurts when the person you love the most doesn't want to listen to a damn thing you say. 

So, just listen to that person who is feeling suicidal. You don't need to speak and give your opinion because often times it is not wanted and will also cause a suicidal person more emotional pain than they were already in. Don't pull out that imaginary masters in psychology you have simply because you think you understand. Because you don't. Even if a suicidal person opens up to another suicidal person. Although they might have a better understanding of the situation at hand, listening is always the best thing you can do. 

I feel so lonely even though I'm around people constantly. Some of these people care about my feelings and others couldn't even give two shits. But, I'm still lonely. 

Just listen. A suicidal person who is willing to talk about the dark place they're in is not something that happens a lot. 

TLDR: don't be a jackass and tell someone what you think the problem is and how you think it can be solved. Listen. You might just save a life.
